key_insight: Analog QAOA on a three-dimensional Rydberg-atom array uses complementary optimization strategies to outperform Goemans–Williamson rounding on nearly all tested weighted MaxCut instances in noiseless simulations.
engineering_relevance: Encoding graph weights in interatomic interactions offers a hardware-oriented route to quantum optimization using global laser control and site-dependent detunings.
method: Choose 3D atom positions to encode problem weights in interaction energies.
Drive trapped Rydberg atoms with global laser pulses and site-dependent detunings.
Combine discretized quantum annealing and graph-neural-network warm starts in an optimization portfolio.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers twenty randomly weighted 3-regular graphs with 12 vertices each, including sampling statistics, pulse-time costs, and quantum-trajectory emulation with a realistic Aquila error model.
watch_item: The reported advantage is noiseless and limited to small simulated benchmarks; noisy hardware performance and scalability remain unestablished.
paper_title: Analog quantum approximate optimization algorithm for solving the weighted MaxCut problem on three-dimensional single-atom Rydberg array
